thread:
amanda: bumping this to #incidents — ClipFast reporting intermittent 504s and p95 token latencies spiking to ~18s across hosted route /v1/generate. Customer-facing errors started ~09:12 UTC and persisted in bursts.
yang: thanks — any sample request_id or stack traces?
amanda: pasted one from support: req=clpf-0a1b2c3d, model=redwood-large-v2, seq_len=1900, concurrency=48. logs show lots of ENQUEUE_WAIT and dequeue timeouts.
ops-bot: alert: route=clipfast-prod queue_depth=1200 continuous_batcher_backlog_ms=2300 host_dequeue_latency_p95=15s
mike: seeing high ENQUEUE_WAIT in host logs: ``[enqueue] req=clpf-0a1b2c3d wait=2350ms batch_size=32``. KV cache misses also spike.
deepa: probable continuous-batching backlog + queue-depth hit. ClipFast is hitting per-route depth limit, requests piling into batcher. Did they recently roll a client change?
amanda: customer says they increased concurrency to 50 when they hit slowdowns earlier. We asked them to revert to 20 but need infra mitigations.
yang: repro steps I used locally: `ab -n 200 -c 40 -p long_prompt.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` with seq_len ~1800 reproduces p95 tail.
mike: quick triage: enable early-reject on route, reduce max-enqueue-depth from 1200->600 for that tenant, and apply temporary rate-limit 30rps. That should reduce queue buildup.
deepa: open question: why continuous-batcher didn't shed earlier — check batching policy thresholds and dequeue loop backpressure. Adding more detail: ``cbatcher: max_inflight_batches=16, enqueue_backpressure_threshold=0.8``. If many large requests, threshold reached fast.
amanda: applying rate-limit and early-reject now (route: clipfast-prod). Will post results shortly.
support-bot: ping to ClipFast — told them we're throttling to mitigate and will follow up after 30m. :thumbsup:
yang: while throttling, I'll collect traces and a pprof of batcher worker to look for dequeue stall or GC pauses.
mike: another mitigation path: enable fallback_model=gpt-small-quant (quantized) for this route for short window — lower throughput per seq but less KV memory pressure.
amanda: fallback enabled at 09:36 UTC and rate-limit at 09:33 UTC. initial effect: 5xxs dropped immediately, p95 fell from 18s->6.8s.
deepa: logged hypothesis to runbook: "continuous-batcher: large-seqlen tenant causing queue-saturation — recommend dynamic per-tenant enqueue cap + early-reject + model-fallback". Adding action items.
yang: captured sample span traces: `enqueue_wait>2s -> batch_create->dequeue_blocked_on_kv=600ms -> model_infer=3s` — indicates KV eviction/rehit cost.
mike: assigned follow-ups: (1) add metric alert for enqueue_backlog_ms>1000 per-route; (2) investigate kvcache eviction tuning; (3) consider adaptive batching knob by seq_len.
amanda: logged customer ticket ID 54823, informed customer of temporary limits and fallback. Customer confirmed degraded but usable.
support-bot: customer updated: errors reduced, throughput stable at reduced concurrency.
yang: will keep on-call for 2h to watch. collecting logs and beginning deeper repro with mixed seq lengths.
deepa: setting up post-incident eval to test thresholds: synthetic runner with variable seq_len mix and concurrency sweep.
amanda: marking thread for follow-up doc and possible config change in prod default batching policy. If stable for 2h, we'll close.
ops-bot: monitor note: route=clipfast-prod enqueue_backlog_ms dropped from 2300->120 then ->90 over 15m after rate-limit+fallback.
amanda: 2h check-in — stable, p95 ~5s, no 504s. I'll open a short postmortem and add runbook step. Thanks everyone. :party:
